title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics across python/typescript/go; parity fixes and version bumps
author: Maya Chen
body: Motivation: This PR unifies auth/retries/streaming ergonomics across the official Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) to reduce surface area for integration bugs, improve developer ergonomics for streaming responses, and ensure parity for retry semantics and configuration. Context: Multiple customer integrations and internal examples showed divergent behaviors between SDKs: auth token refresh handling varied, retry backoff semantics were inconsistent, and streaming APIs had slightly different function/handler shapes which made cross-language reference apps brittle. Changes: 1) Auth: centralize bearer token refresh hooks and standardize default 401->refresh->retry logic; expose a single credentials interface pattern across SDKs. 2) Retries: implement identical retry policy primitives (max_attempts, base_backoff_ms, jitter) and deterministic idempotency detection for requests with streaming vs non-streaming payloads. 3) Streaming API ergonomics: provide unified streaming iterator/callback signatures and a small helper for converting low-level frames to user-level events. 4) Parity fixes: align TypeScript error types with Python, ensure Go returns typed errors for known status classes, add consistent metadata fields to stream events. 5) Version bumps: update package versions to Python 1.14.0, TypeScript 1.8.2, Go v0.9.0; include changelogs and migration notes. Non-functional: add end-to-end regression tests that run a cross-SDK test matrix in CI, add docs examples to quickstarts. Checklist: ensure backwards compatibility where possible, add deprecation notes for removed helpers, update changelogs, run full CI, coordinate release. Testing: unit tests in each SDK, integration tests against the local redwood test harness, cross-language streaming smoke tests, manual verification of token refresh under race conditions. Rollout plan: staged releases starting with Python (canary beta opt-in), then TS, then Go; feature flags for enabling new retry defaults. Migration: most users will be unaffected; if users override retry internals they may need to update to the new primitive names. Notes: This PR consolidates shared behavior but keeps language idioms intact (async iterators in Python/TS, channels in Go). See linked Linear items for design discussion and benchmarks.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Overall this looks good. A couple of nits: can we rename base_backoff_ms to base_backoff_ms_or_s so the units are clear? Also add a short example for custom retry policies.
Maya Chen: Thanks Arjun — I standardized the name to base_backoff_ms (ms is used throughout the repo) and added a note in the comments and CHANGELOG. Example added to docs/quickstarts.
Sofia Martinez: In typescript stream helpers the event shape differs slightly from python (python uses 'type'/'payload', ts used 'eventType'/'data'). Please normalize to 'type'/'data' for parity.
Maya Chen: Normalized TS to 'type'/'data' and updated examples. Added a compatibility helper for older consumers.

Benji O'Neill: CI showed a flaky test in Go around token refresh race (test_token_refresh_race). I think we need to add a small jitter in the refresh path to avoid thundering herd under test harness. Please add a comment and a small exponential backoff jitter.
Maya Chen: Added jitter and comment, and added an explicit test asserting no double-refresh under parallel calls. The CI run passed this time.
Arjun Patel: Approved after the last fixes.
Release lead (Lina Gomez): Please coordinate publishing order and update the release calendar. All good from SRE perspective.
release_notes: Unify auth token refresh handling and retry primitives across SDKs. Improve streaming ergonomics and event parity between Python, TypeScript, and Go. Version bumps: python 1.14.0, typescript 1.8.2, go v0.9.0. See CHANGELOGs for migration notes.
notes: Backwards-compatible defaults preserved; advanced users replacing retry internals may need small updates
Canary rollout for Python before TS/Go to monitor client-side telemetry
Added cross-sdk e2e tests to CI to prevent regressions
short_description: Unify SDK auth/retries/streaming APIs across Python/TS/Go, add parity fixes and bump versions. Includes tests and docs updates.
